part1_forecasts.statement: The U.S. will collect over $500 million in tariff revenue from advanced AI chip imports by the end of 2027, based on the 25% tariff imposed in January 2026.

resolution_criteria.metric: Total tariff revenue from advanced AI chips

part1_forecasts.statement: Foreign direct investment into U.S. AI infrastructure, incentivized by export controls like those in E05, will exceed $10 billion in 2028.

resolution_criteria.source: U.S. Department of Commerce, Bureau of Economic Analysis
resolution_criteria.metric: Foreign direct investment in U.S. AI infrastructure
resolution_criteria.counting_convention: USD; annual FDI inflow specifically categorized under AI infrastructure

part1_forecasts.statement: The U.S. AI chip industry's domestic production capacity will increase by at least 15% by 2029 due to government policies aimed at fostering domestic production, as outlined in the Modern Mercantilism framework.

resolution_criteria.source: U.S. Department of Commerce, Semiconductor Industry Association
resolution_criteria.counting_convention: percentage increase; year-over-year growth in wafer starts or output

part1_forecasts.statement: OpenAI's API credits offered as part of its industrial policy framework will be fully utilized by at least 50 research institutions globally by the end of 2027.

resolution_criteria.metric: Number of research institutions utilizing API credits
resolution_criteria.counting_convention: count; institutions fully utilizing credits for research purposes

part1_forecasts.statement: Lobbying expenditures by companies like AMD and KLA Corp. focused on AI trade and export controls will cumulatively exceed $10 million by the end of 2027.

resolution_criteria.metric: Cumulative lobbying expenditures on AI trade and export controls
resolution_criteria.counting_convention: USD; sum of disclosed lobbying expenditures by specified companies

part1_forecasts.statement: U.S. productivity growth will average at least 1.8% annually between 2027 and 2030, indicating a potential improvement due to targeted AI industrial policy.
The U.S. Department of Commerce will adjust its license review policy for high-end chip exports at least three more times by the end of 2029 to further refine strategic selectivity.

resolution_criteria.source: U.S. Department of Commerce, Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS)
resolution_criteria.metric: Number of policy adjustments to high-end chip export license review
resolution_criteria.counting_convention: count; formal rule changes or policy statements by BIS

part1_forecasts.statement: At least five countries will publicly commit to matching investments in American AI infrastructure as a condition for significant AI chip cluster builds by the end of 2028, mirroring the tiered export control regulations.

resolution_criteria.source: Department of State, Bilateral Agreements Database
resolution_criteria.metric: Number of countries making matching investment commitments for AI infrastructure
resolution_criteria.counting_convention: count; public bilateral or multilateral agreements specifying matching investment

part1_forecasts.statement: The global venture investment in AI will grow by at least 50% from its 2026 level by the end of 2031, driven by continued state-led industrial policy and AI development.

The U.S. will successfully implement at least two new bilateral AI supply chain security agreements with key allies by the end of 2028, reinforcing the strategic competition aspect of Modern Mercantilism.

resolution_criteria.metric: Number of bilateral AI supply chain security agreements
